'The vl. stops /p/ and /t/ occur in all dialects in all positions' (§9.2): **telu > SB, Si tolu, NB telu 'three'; 'I reconstruct *p and *t'. NB c for *t only before i (§9.4.1). Entered with the next row so that the c row does not stand alone.

'Si, SB /t/ corresponds to NB /c/ before /i/': **kutiŋ 'cat' > SB, Si hutiŋ, Ka kuciŋ, Da kəciŋ; **tikep > Ka cikap (§9.4.1). Adelaar reconstructs *t 'because a development from *t to /c/ is much more common than one from *c to /t/'.
'*e from /ə/ in Ka, /ə/ and /o/ in Da, /o/ in Si-SB' (§7.2.4): **enem > SB-Si onom, NB ənəm; a common innovation of Si and SB (§9.3.1d).
NB /k/ : To, An h~k, Ma k~Ø, Si h~k (§9.3): **kutu > SB, Si hutu, Ma [utu], NB kutu. 'Si agrees with SB in its change of *k to /h/ in initial and medial position' (§9.3.1a).
NB /h/ corresponds to Ø-, -Ø-, -Ø in SB and to Ø-, -Ø-, -h in Si (§9.3): **tabeh > SB tabo, Si taboh; Si and SB share the loss of *h 'except in final position, where it is retained in Si' (§9.3.1a).
Retained in Si only: **si-ba(e)seh > Si si-basoh, SB si-baso (§9.3).
SB -Ø for NB, Si -h (§9.3): **pereh > SB poro, Si poroh, Ka pereh.
'PB *c became /s/ in both SB and Si' (§9.3.1c, §9.4.1): **racun > SB, Si rasun, NB racun; AnMa have s~c.
'Da does not allow /ə/ before fin. /h/ and in monosyll. lexemes, and has /o/ instead' (§7.2.4): **taneh > Da tanoh, Ka tanəh.
